import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a categorical plot to show survival rate by gender and passenger class
# 'survived' is a binary variable (0 or 1), so the mean directly represents the survival rate.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='sex',
    y='survived',
    hue='pclass',
    kind='point',  # Point plot is excellent for displaying means and confidence intervals
    palette='viridis', # A colorblind-friendly palette
    errorbar='ci', # Show 95% confidence interval
    height=6,      # Height of the plot
    aspect=1.2     # Aspect ratio of the plot
)

# Set the main title for the figure
g.fig.suptitle('Survival Rate by Gender and Passenger Class on the Titanic', y=1.03, fontsize=16)

# Set axis labels
g.set_axis_labels('Gender', 'Survival Rate')

# Improve the legend title for clarity
g._legend.set_title('Passenger Class')

# Set y-axis limits to clearly represent a rate from 0 to 1
g.set(ylim=(0, 1))

# Add grid for better readability
g.ax.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd

    data=df,
    x='sex',

    hue='pclass',
    kind='point',  # Point plot is excellent for displaying means and confidence intervals
    palette='viridis', # A colorblind-friendly palette

g.fig.suptitle('Survival Rate by Gender and Passenger Class on the Titanic', y=1.03, fontsize=16)
